newsitem.title: UK: Dollar surges to fresh highs in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar surges to fresh highs in late Europe.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 10 Reuter) - The dollar surged to fresh 29-month highs against the mark in late European trade, bolstered by renewed speculation of higher U.S. interest rates following robust U.S. jobs data.

The dollar rose to a session high of 1.5865 marks, a level not seen since August 1994. The dollar's strength also spilled over to the Swiss franc and French franc which registered 31-month and two-year highs respectively.
The strong payrolls data depressed the U.S. stock and bond markets but the dollar took heart from the strengthening U.S. economy against the backdrop of sluggish performance from Germany and Japan.

"The payrolls data has added fuel to the idea the U.S. economy is overheating and the Fed will be forced to tighten," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London. "We don't think the Fed will raise rates in February but a rate hike is not ruled at the March FOMC."
By 1615 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5850/55 marks after touching earlier its fresh peak at 1.5858 but still well above late Thursday's European level of 1.5773/78 marks.
Dollar/Swiss franc stood at 1.3750/60 from a peak of 1.3783 francs and against the French franc it was at 5.3482/92 after touching 5.3510 earlier.
Dealers said trade was lively in Europe pre- and post-payroll data.
"The dollar has been bid across the board this afternoon, particulary after the data and this looks set to continue -- there are still a lot of shorts out there," said a Japanese bank dealer.
The dollar was also firmer against the yen as it followed dollar/mark's progress higher but was still shy of the 116 yen level.
At 1626 GMT, it was trading at 115.90/95 from 116.26/31 late Thursday in Europe.
The dollar/mark surge pushed the mark lower on the European currencies in afternoon trade with mark/lira testing at fresh 31-month low.
The mark was off an earlier four-year low against the Norwegian crown, its earlier slide accelerated by the Norwegian central bank's decision not to intervene to dampen the crown's strength.
The Norwegian central bank also cut interest rates for the second time in a week, lowering its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 3.25 percent.
